products.note: Research discovery AI; paper recommendations; collaboration features; academic data

reading.body:
ResearchRabbit is a research discovery tool that reduces the time academics spend on literature reviews by automating paper recommendations and citation mapping rather than replacing researcher judgment.

The platform surfaces related papers through bibliographic analysis and co-author relationships, then refines its recommendations as users select papers. This is a narrow but real efficiency gain in knowledge work: it accelerates the filtering stage of research but does not generate novel insights. The collaboration features suggest the tool is built for teams, not solitary researchers, which may increase adoption in institutional settings.

This product consumes minimal compute relative to large language models. It operates on structured academic metadata rather than training on unfiltered text, and its recommendations appear algorithmic rather than inference-based. The data does not indicate whether the company operates its own infrastructure or relies on cloud providers, so the power and buildings footprint remains unknown. What matters here is that efficiency tools in knowledge work are proliferating in the AI ecosystem without requiring the scale of compute that generative models demand.

The absence of litigation, patents, or regulatory filings suggests the company operates without major technical disputes or capital raises large enough to trigger SEC disclosure. This leaves open how it funds operations and whether its data licensing agreements with academic publishers or databases pose competitive or legal risks down the line.

profile_text.body:
ResearchRabbit is an AI-powered research discovery tool designed to help academics and researchers conduct literature reviews more efficiently. The platform allows users to find related academic papers, build citation maps, and track research trends, with the goal of reducing the time spent on manual literature searches. According to the site, the tool analyzes bibliographies, citations, and co-author relationships to surface related articles, and its algorithm refines recommendations as users select papers, learning their interests over time.

The product is described by users at Sam Houston State University as helping researchers visualize connections between existing research and streamline the discovery of related work, with the potential to reduce the burden of comprehensive literature reviews. ResearchRabbit also includes collaboration features, allowing researchers to work together within the platform.

The site's held facts list one product under the search and research category, also called ResearchRabbit, with noted capabilities including paper recommendations, collaboration features, and access to academic data. No litigation, SEC filings, patents, or MCP server registrations are recorded for the company.
